```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

#Question 1

```{r}
bdays = sample(1:365, 25, replace = TRUE)

length(unique(bdays)) < 25
```

```{r}
bday = function(n) {
  if (!is.numeric(n)) {
    stop("n must be numerical")
  } else if (n<2) {
    stop("group has at least 2 ppl")
  }
  
  bdays = sample (1:365, n, replace = TRUE)
  
  any(duplicated(bdays))
}

bday(10)
bday(50)
```

```{r}
bday_function_df =
  expand.grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared = map_lgl(group_size, bday)
  )

prob_df =
  bday_function_df |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarise(prob_shared = mean(shared))
```


```{r}
prob_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob_shared)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of shared birthday",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Probability of shared birthday"
  )
```
The probability of a shared birthday rises steadily as group size increases. The smaller the group size is, the lower probability there is of having a shared birthday. It reaches 50% probability at around a group size of 23 and increases to 96% probability at a group size of 48 and plateaus afterwards.


#Question 2

```{r}
data_df = "data/data/"

participant_df =
  tibble(
    files = list.files(data_df),
    path = str_c(data_df, files)
  ) |>
  mutate(data = map(path, read_csv)) |>
  unnest(cols = data)
```

```{r}
tidy_df =
  participant_df |>
  mutate(
    files = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    arm = str_sub(files, 1,3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week))|>
  select(arm, subj = files,week, outcome)
```
This is the tidy dataset with `r nrow(tidy_df)` rows and `r ncol(tidy_df)` columns. The variables of the columns are `r names(tidy_df)`. Depicting the arm (control vs experimental) a participant is in, the participant subject ID, week, and outcome data.

## Spaghetti plot
```{r}
tidy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subj, color = arm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~arm) +
  labs(
    title = "Outcome of each participant over time",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome",
    color = "Arm"
  )
```
Particpants in the control arm begin with outcome measures between 0 and 2.5. Participants in the experimental arm begin with outcome measures around the same level between -1 and 3.75. Over time, participants in the control arm remain relatively steady with outcome measures that remain fairly constant. By Week 8, outcome measure remain between around 0 and 2.5. However, for the experimental arm, over time outcome measures increase steadily for all participants. By Week 8, outcome measure rise between 2.5 and 7.5.

#Question 3

```{r}
t_test_df = function(mu, n = 30, sigma = 5) {
  
  test_data_df = tibble(
    x = rnorm(n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  )
  test_data_df |>
    pull(x) |>
    t.test(mu = 0) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}
```

```{r}
model_df =
  expand_grid(
    mu = 0:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    results_df = map(mu, t_test_df)
  ) |>
  unnest(results_df) |>
  mutate(reject = p.value < 0.05)
```

## Plot for true value of mu vs rejection of null proportions
```{r}
rejection_df =
  model_df |>
  group_by(mu) |>
  summarise(power = mean(reject))

rejection_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = power)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "True Value of Mu vs Power",
    x = "True Value of Mu",
    y = "Proportion of times the null was rejected (Power)"
  )
```

At an effect size of 0, the power equals about 0.05. The curve continues to rise steadily, showing that as the true value of mu (effect size) increases, the proportion of times the null is rejected (power) increases. The curve then levels and plateaus at a true mu value of 4, with a power of 1, meaning the test almost always rejects the null after this point.

```{r}
average_df = 
  model_df |>
  group_by(mu) |>
  summarise(avg_estimate = mean(estimate)) |>
  mutate(samples = "All samples")

average_rejected_df =
  model_df |>
  filter(reject) |>
  group_by(mu) |>
  summarise(avg_estimate = mean(estimate)) |>
    mutate(samples = "Rejected null")

bind_rows(average_df, average_rejected_df) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mu, y = avg_estimate, color = samples)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "True Value of Mu x Average Estimate of Mu, for All Samples vs. Samples For Which the Null Was Rejected",
    x = "True value of mu",
    y = "Average estimate of mu",
    color = "samples"
  )
```
For mu= 1 and mu =2, the sample average of mu across tests for which the null is rejected is larger than that of the true value of mu. As mu increases, the sample average of mu across tests for which the null is rejected approximately equals to the true value of mu. This is seen at mu values of 4 and above.
